reading.body:
Connecticut's tracked 2026 legislative bills split between AI specific measures, an artificial intelligence small business development plan, a task force on AI's effects on the trades industry, an automated decision systems law protecting employees, a deceptive synthetic media and elections bill, and a broader responsible AI innovation act, and a larger set of bills that only mention AI in passing within omnibus legislation covering consumer protection, cannabis, data privacy, and fire inspections together.

That an AI provision appears folded into a single bill alongside cannabis regulation, fire inspections, and criminal mischief shows how state legislatures sometimes attach AI language to unrelated must pass legislation rather than advancing it as a standalone measure.

The employee focused automated decision systems bill and the elections focused synthetic media bill represent the two clearest single purpose AI measures in this list, addressing workplace algorithmic management and election integrity respectively as distinct policy problems.

The data does not indicate which of these 19 bills passed, failed, or remain pending, nor does it include bill text beyond title and number, so Connecticut's actual AI legal framework as enacted is not established by this record.
